R7BK-bear-drive-0001.name: 4.5 km SW of Kiwigana River
R7BK-bear-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7BK-bear-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2006 (20 years old), 30 m NE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire G90207), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Unnamed wetland right here: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Old Fort Nelson, about 84 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.3501, -123.01928, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 200 m N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 3 m, about 5 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-55, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
